reason: 2.1.1 transitions an input's background-color, border-color, color and box-shadow but not its border-width. A checked radio is a 0.35em border around a --femto-primary-inverse background, so on uncheck the border snaps back to --femto-border-width at once while the background fades to the form background over 0.2s. For about 150ms the whole radio is a disc in the dot's color, which neither state shows: white in the dark scheme, and black in the light scheme with the amber, grey, lime, pumpkin, sand and yellow themes. femto leaves background-color out of an unchecked radio's transition-property, so the background takes the unchecked color at once while the border color, text color and focus ring still fade. Checking still fades the dot in, because the thick border is already in place. The one other effect is that a scheme flip no longer fades an unchecked radio's background. The rule is input:where([type=radio]:not(:checked)) in forms/checkbox-radio-switch.css, at the (0,0,1) of the input transition rule in forms/basics.css and after it, so an author's own transition rule on inputs or radios loaded after femto still wins, and the no-transitions option's input reset, at the same specificity and loaded later, restores transition-property all, so that preset matches the 2.1.1 no-transitions build and shows no difference.
notes: Fixtures: every unchecked radio in the harness pages, which are the only ones listed in where.pages: #r-2 (hover, focus, active), the disabled #r-3 and the "Unchecked invalid" radio in forms-checkbox-radio-switch.html, the aria-invalid=false "Valid radio" (focus) and the fs-radio fieldset radio in forms-basics.html, the g-radio radio in components-group.html, the "Option two" radio in classes-dropdown.html and #ks-r2 in kitchen-sink.html. Checked radios, checkboxes and switches are unchanged, and resting screenshots are identical. The harness finishes transitions before comparing, so it shows only the computed property; the flash was probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta, data-theme dark and light and no data-theme with preferred dark and light, ltr and rtl, at 1000 and 390px, unchecking a radio and pausing the transitions at 0, 50, 100 and 150ms. 2.1.1 and femto before the fix in the dark scheme: rgb(255, 255, 255) at 0ms, #e2e2e4 at 50ms, rgb(142, 144, 149) (Chrome) or rgb(142, 144, 150) (Firefox) at 100ms, #393e47 at 150ms, with every pixel inside the 2px border more than 48 luminance above the settled fill until 100ms, and a real click peaking 222.3 above it; amber in the light scheme: #000000, then rgb(126, 126, 126) at 100ms, peaking 251.8 below the fill. femto: rgb(28, 33, 44) in the dark scheme and rgb(251, 252, 252) in the light one in every frame, peak 0, in both browsers. Checking still fades background-color and the four border colors, and an author input or [type=radio] transition rule loaded after femto computes as before. Reduced motion and no-transitions never flashed. Upstream issue picocss/pico#502.

reason: A switch draws its thumb with ::before, and 2.1.1's tooltip rules also match that ::before. The thumb rule outranks the base tooltip rule only on content, background and radius, so with data-tooltip 2.1.1 made the thumb position: absolute and opacity: 0, moved it above the switch with the tooltip's translate, and gave it the tooltip's padding and 0.875rem font size. At rest the switch had no thumb. On hover or focus the thumb slid in above the switch as a blank shape with the tooltip's caret (::after), and a checked switch's shape sat off-center, because its 1em margin used the smaller font size. With data-placement=top the tooltip also won on content, background and radius, so the shape took the tooltip color and held a clipped scrap of the text. No usable tooltip ever showed. femto keeps the thumb on a switch with data-tooltip and hides the caret, so the switch renders exactly like one without data-tooltip and shows no tooltip. Two rules in forms/checkbox-radio-switch.css restore the thumb's position, padding, transform, radius, color, content, font size, opacity and animation, at (0,3,1) and, with :focus and :hover, (0,4,1), above every tooltip rule, options/no-transitions.css included, and set display: none on the ::after. A tooltip for a switch goes on its label, which already worked and is unchanged.
notes: Fixtures: the three switches with data-tooltip in the Switches fieldset of forms-checkbox-radio-switch.html: s-tip (checked, hover and focus), s-tip-bottom (checked, data-placement=bottom, hover and focus) and s-tip-top (unchecked, data-placement=top). The harness records only their ::before and ::after; the inputs themselves and the plain switches, checkboxes and radios around them show no difference. The harness screenshots cover the top 800px, which these switches sit below, so the picture was probed with a standalone Selenium page in Chrome 158 and Firefox 160 beta: each of 12 tooltipped switches (off, on, every placement, rtl, a data-theme=dark wrapper, a 12px font size, aria-invalid, disabled) rendered alone at one spot next to an identical switch without data-tooltip, at rest, on hover and on focus, in light, dark and light with reduced motion, at 1400 and 600px, with and without options/no-transitions.css. 2.1.1 and femto before the fix matched the plain switch in none of the 36 cells of any configuration in either browser, with up to 723 pixels differing. At rest the checked thumb's ::before computed position absolute, opacity 0, transform matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, -10, -5), padding 5px 10px and font-size 17.5px against the input's 20px, so its 1em margin was 17.5px, and the ::after was display block; on hover and focus the ::before ran tooltip-slide to opacity 1 and the caret showed. With the fix every cell matches with 0 differing pixels in both browsers (180 of 180, and 72 of 72 with no-transitions), the computed ::before (position, opacity, transform, font size, margins, padding, animation, content, background, radius, size) equals the plain switch's, and the ::after is display none. A span, checkbox, button and label with data-tooltip are pixel-identical before and after the fix (96 of 96 crops). Upstream issue picocss/pico#629, whose dotted underline on a tooltipped label is the designed affordance and stays.
